title: BMW bumps battery for the better: The 2027 i7 60 xDrive, driven
gist: BMW's mid-life update moves its i7 flagship to the sixth-generation (Neue Klasse) electric powertrain: a 112.5 kWh cylindrical-cell pack, silicon carbide inverters, 250 kW charging (still 400 V), 344-362 miles of claimed range, NACS, and domain controllers. Its 4.6 s 0-60 time is now slow next to Lucid, Tesla, Porsche, and Chinese EVs, and pricing starts at $106,200.

themes.theme: BMW Gen6 powertrain trickles up to flagship

insights.claim: BMW's sixth-generation electric powertrain switched from prismatic to more energy-dense cylindrical cells and added silicon carbide inverters with more compact drive units, while keeping electrically excited synchronous motors.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: Adoption of cylindrical cells and SiC inverters by a major European automaker supports demand for those suppliers.
insights.locator: Since then, BMW has brought out

insights.claim: BMW's Neue Klasse architecture replaces dozens of single-function electronic control units with a handful of powerful domain controllers that are faster and easier to update.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: Legacy automakers moving to centralized, software-defined vehicle architectures benefits automotive chip and software suppliers.

insights.claim: BMW upgraded the i7 at its mid-life update so the flagship would not be outclassed in power, energy density, and efficiency by its newer, cheaper Neue Klasse EVs.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: Fast EV technology cycles force automakers to make expensive mid-cycle updates so their flagships keep up.

insights.claim: The 2027 BMW i7 has a 112.5 kWh net battery, up from 101.7 kWh, but keeps a 400 V architecture, with DC fast charging rising to 250 kW from 195 kW and a 10-80 percent charge taking about 28 minutes.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: Staying at 400 V puts the flagship behind 800 V competitors on charging, a cost-saving tradeoff.

insights.claim: BMW claims 344 to 362 miles of range for the 2027 i7 depending on wheel size, and like other model-year 2027 BMW EVs it uses a NACS charging port.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: Adoption of NACS across the industry strengthens Tesla's charging network.

insights.claim: BMW uses AI simulations of the battery based on previous charging cycles to plan routes and choose charging stops, factoring in the cost per kWh at different stations.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: Software features like cost-aware charging are becoming ways for automakers to differentiate their EVs.

themes.theme: Luxury EV performance commoditized by rivals

insights.claim: The 2027 BMW i7 60 xDrive's 0-60 mph time of 4.6 seconds is now more than double that of electric sedans from Lucid, Tesla, Porsche, and many Chinese automakers.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: Acceleration no longer sets EVs apart, so luxury brands have to compete on comfort and refinement, with Chinese automakers setting the performance pace.
insights.quote: electric sedans from Lucid and Tesla and Porsche and a whole load of Chinese automakers will get you there in less than half the i7’s time

insights.claim: BMW offers the 7 Series with a choice of V8 or electric powertrain in one body rather than a separate EV model, unlike Mercedes' split between EQS and S-Class.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: Offering multiple powertrains on one platform lowers BMW's risk if EV adoption is uneven.

insights.claim: The 2027 BMW i7 starts at $106,200 for the 50 xDrive and $124,700 for the 60 xDrive.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: This price range puts the i7 up against the Lucid Air and the EQS.

insights.claim: Despite a new infotainment domain controller, the 2027 i7 still showed noticeable lag on its main screen, while its Alexa-based voice recognition was notably improved over the iX3 a few months earlier.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: Amazon's Alexa is gaining a place in premium car voice assistants, although automakers still struggle with software performance.
